subject: biology
note: One revision note per concept. Each GCSE spec point is primary in exactly one concept; non-primary refs are broad points that also need this note.

concepts.title: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
concepts.scope: Compares eukaryotic (animal, plant) and prokaryotic (bacterial) cells, including plasmids, size and order of magnitude.

concepts.title: Animal and plant cell structures
concepts.scope: The sub-cellular structures of animal and plant cells (nucleus, membrane, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts, wall, vacuole) and their functions.

concepts.title: Cell specialisation and differentiation
concepts.scope: How cells differentiate and how specialised cells such as sperm, egg, nerve, muscle, root hair, xylem and phloem cells are adapted to their functions.

concepts.title: Growth and percentile charts
concepts.scope: Growth by cell division, elongation and differentiation in plants and animals, and using percentile charts to monitor growth.

concepts.title: Light and electron microscopes
concepts.scope: How light and electron microscopes compare in magnification and resolution, staining, and how electron microscopy improved understanding of sub-cellular structures.

concepts.title: Magnification calculations and units
concepts.scope: Using magnification = image size / actual size, converting between mm, um and nm, and using standard form and estimation for cell sizes.

concepts.title: Required practical: using a light microscope
concepts.scope: Preparing slides and observing cells with a light microscope, making labelled drawings and calculating magnification.

concepts.title: Chromosomes, mitosis and the cell cycle
concepts.scope: Chromosomes and genes, the stages of the cell cycle and mitosis, and its role in growth, repair and asexual reproduction producing identical diploid cells.

concepts.title: Stem cells
concepts.scope: What stem cells are, where they are found (embryos, adult bone marrow, plant meristems) and the difference between embryonic and adult stem cells.

concepts.title: Stem cells in medicine and plant cloning
concepts.scope: Uses of stem cells in treating disease, therapeutic cloning, meristems for cloning plants, and the benefits, risks and ethical issues.

concepts.title: Diffusion
concepts.scope: Diffusion of substances into and out of cells and the factors that affect its rate (concentration gradient, temperature, surface area, distance).

concepts.title: Osmosis
concepts.scope: Osmosis as the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane, water potential, and its effects on plant and animal cells.

concepts.title: Required practical: osmosis in plant tissue
concepts.scope: Investigating the effect of solution concentration on the mass of potato pieces and calculating percentage change in mass.

concepts.title: Active transport
concepts.scope: Moving substances against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration, e.g. mineral ions into root hairs and glucose into gut cells, compared with diffusion and osmosis.

concepts.title: Exchange surfaces and surface area to volume ratio
concepts.scope: Why multicellular organisms need exchange surfaces and transport systems, calculating SA:V, Fick's law, and the substances organisms exchange.

concepts.title: Culturing microorganisms and aseptic technique
concepts.scope: Bacterial growth by binary fission, aseptic technique for culturing microorganisms, calculating bacterial numbers and areas of inhibition zones.

concepts.title: Required practical: effect of antiseptics and antibiotics on bacteria
concepts.scope: Investigating how antiseptics, antibiotics or plant extracts affect bacterial growth by measuring clear zones on agar plates.

concepts.title: Levels of organisation
concepts.scope: How cells, tissues, organs and organ systems are organised in multicellular organisms.

concepts.title: The human digestive system
concepts.scope: The organs of the digestive system and how they work together to digest and absorb food.

concepts.title: Enzymes and the lock-and-key model
concepts.scope: Enzymes as biological catalysts, the active site, specificity and the lock-and-key model.

concepts.title: Factors affecting enzyme activity
concepts.scope: How temperature, pH and substrate concentration affect enzyme activity, denaturation, and calculating rates of enzyme reactions.

concepts.title: Required practical: effect of pH on amylase
concepts.scope: Investigating how pH affects the rate at which amylase breaks down starch, using iodine and continuous sampling.

concepts.title: Digestive enzymes
concepts.scope: Carbohydrases, proteases and lipases, where they are made and what they produce, plus bile and the use of digestion products to build new molecules.

concepts.title: Required practical: food tests
concepts.scope: Using iodine, Benedict's, biuret and the emulsion (or Sudan III) test to identify starch, sugars, proteins and lipids.

concepts.title: Measuring energy in food (calorimetry)
concepts.scope: Measuring the energy content of food by burning it and heating water, and calculating energy per gram.

concepts.title: The lungs and gas exchange
concepts.scope: The structure of the breathing system and how alveoli are adapted for gas exchange by diffusion.

concepts.title: The heart and double circulation
concepts.scope: The structure of the heart, its chambers, valves and major vessels, the double circulatory system and the pacemaker.

concepts.title: Cardiac output
concepts.scope: Calculating cardiac output from stroke volume and heart rate.

concepts.title: Blood vessels
concepts.scope: How the structures of arteries, veins and capillaries relate to their functions.

concepts.title: Blood
concepts.scope: The components of blood (plasma, red cells, white cells, platelets) and how they are adapted to their functions.

concepts.title: Coronary heart disease and its treatments
concepts.scope: How fatty deposits cause coronary heart disease and the evaluation of treatments: statins, stents, bypass, valve replacement, transplants and lifestyle changes.

concepts.title: Health and disease
concepts.scope: What health means, communicable versus non-communicable disease, and how diseases interact (e.g. HIV and TB, HPV and cervical cancer).

concepts.title: Risk factors and lifestyle in non-communicable disease
concepts.scope: How lifestyle factors such as diet, exercise, smoking and alcohol interact to cause non-communicable diseases, including BMI and waist-to-hip calculations and their costs.

concepts.title: Cancer
concepts.scope: Cancer as uncontrolled cell division, benign and malignant tumours, and risk factors.

concepts.title: Plant tissues and leaf structure
concepts.scope: The tissues in a leaf (epidermis, palisade and spongy mesophyll, xylem, phloem, meristem) and how the leaf is adapted for photosynthesis and gas exchange.

concepts.title: Root hair cells, xylem and phloem
concepts.scope: How root hair cells take up water and minerals and how xylem and phloem are adapted for transport in the plant.

concepts.title: Transpiration and stomata
concepts.scope: Transpiration as water loss from leaves and movement through the xylem, and how guard cells open and close stomata.

concepts.title: Factors affecting transpiration and the potometer
concepts.scope: How light, temperature, air movement and humidity affect transpiration rate and how to measure water uptake with a potometer.

concepts.title: Translocation
concepts.scope: Movement of dissolved sugars from source to sink through the phloem.

concepts.title: Pathogens and how disease spreads
concepts.scope: The four types of pathogen and how communicable diseases spread and can be prevented in animals and plants.

concepts.title: Viral diseases
concepts.scope: Viral diseases such as measles, HIV and tobacco mosaic virus: symptoms, spread and control.

concepts.title: Bacterial diseases
concepts.scope: Bacterial diseases such as salmonella, gonorrhoea, cholera, tuberculosis and Helicobacter: symptoms, spread and control.

concepts.title: Fungal and protist diseases
concepts.scope: Fungal and protist diseases such as rose black spot, ash dieback and malaria, and how their spread is controlled.

concepts.title: Sexually transmitted infections
concepts.scope: How STIs such as chlamydia and HIV are spread and how their spread is reduced.

concepts.title: Viral life cycles: lytic and lysogenic
concepts.scope: How viruses reproduce by the lytic and lysogenic pathways.

concepts.title: Non-specific human defences
concepts.scope: The body's physical and chemical barriers to pathogens: skin, mucus, cilia, stomach acid and lysozymes.

concepts.title: The immune system and white blood cells
concepts.scope: How white blood cells defend the body by phagocytosis, antibodies and antitoxins, and how memory lymphocytes give immunity.

concepts.title: Vaccination
concepts.scope: How vaccines trigger immunity and the advantages and disadvantages of vaccination programmes, including herd immunity.

concepts.title: Antibiotics and painkillers
concepts.scope: Why antibiotics kill bacteria but not viruses, the role of painkillers, antivirals and antiseptics in treating and preventing disease.

concepts.title: Discovery and development of drugs
concepts.scope: Where drugs come from and how new medicines are tested through preclinical and clinical trials, including double-blind trials and placebos.

concepts.title: Producing monoclonal antibodies
concepts.scope: How monoclonal antibodies are made by fusing lymphocytes with tumour cells to form hybridoma cells.

concepts.title: Uses of monoclonal antibodies
concepts.scope: Using monoclonal antibodies in pregnancy tests, diagnosis, research and treating cancer, and their side effects.

concepts.title: Detecting and identifying plant diseases
concepts.scope: Signs of plant disease and ion deficiencies, and how plant diseases are identified in the field and the lab.

concepts.title: Plant defence responses
concepts.scope: Physical, chemical and mechanical defences plants use against pathogens and pests.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis
concepts.scope: The photosynthesis equation, photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction in chloroplasts, and plants and algae as producers of biomass.

concepts.title: Limiting factors of photosynthesis
concepts.scope: How light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature and chlorophyll limit the rate of photosynthesis, read from graphs.

concepts.title: Interacting limiting factors and the inverse square law
concepts.scope: How limiting factors interact, the inverse square law for light intensity, and using limiting factors to manage greenhouses economically.

concepts.title: Required practical: light intensity and rate of photosynthesis
concepts.scope: Investigating how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis using pondweed or algal balls.

concepts.title: Uses of glucose from photosynthesis
concepts.scope: How plants use glucose for respiration, starch, fats and oils, cellulose and amino acids.

concepts.title: Aerobic respiration
concepts.scope: Respiration as a continuous exothermic reaction supplying energy (ATP) for living processes, and the aerobic respiration equation.

concepts.title: Anaerobic respiration and fermentation
concepts.scope: Anaerobic respiration in muscles and in plants and yeast, comparing its products and energy yield with aerobic respiration.

concepts.title: Required practical: rate of respiration
concepts.scope: Measuring the rate of respiration of small organisms using a respirometer.

concepts.title: Response to exercise
concepts.scope: How heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume change during exercise, oxygen debt and lactic acid.

concepts.title: Metabolism
concepts.scope: Metabolism as the sum of all reactions, including building and breaking down carbohydrates, proteins and lipids from their monomers.

concepts.title: Principles of homeostasis
concepts.scope: Why a constant internal environment matters and how control systems use receptors, coordination centres and effectors.

concepts.title: The nervous system
concepts.scope: The structure of the nervous system, neurones and synapses, and how a stimulus leads to a coordinated response.

concepts.title: Reflex actions
concepts.scope: The reflex arc and why reflexes are rapid and automatic.

concepts.title: The brain
concepts.scope: The main regions of the brain (cerebral cortex, cerebellum, medulla, hypothalamus, pituitary) and their functions.

concepts.title: Studying the brain and treating nervous system damage
concepts.scope: How scientists investigate brain function (patients, electrical stimulation, CT and PET scans) and why brain and spinal damage is hard to treat.

concepts.title: The eye
concepts.scope: The structure of the eye, accommodation and the pupil reflex.

concepts.title: Eye defects and their correction
concepts.scope: Short- and long-sightedness, cataracts and colour blindness, and how lenses and surgery correct them.

concepts.title: Control of body temperature
concepts.scope: How the hypothalamus and skin control body temperature by sweating, shivering, vasodilation and vasoconstriction.

concepts.title: The endocrine system
concepts.scope: The endocrine glands, the hormones they release and how hormones travel in the blood to target organs, compared with nerves.

concepts.title: Control of blood glucose
concepts.scope: How the pancreas uses insulin and glucagon to keep blood glucose concentration constant by negative feedback.

concepts.title: Diabetes
concepts.scope: The causes and treatments of type 1 and type 2 diabetes and the link between obesity, BMI and type 2 diabetes.

concepts.title: Water and nitrogen balance
concepts.scope: Why water, ion and urea levels must be controlled, how urea is made from excess amino acids, and the effect of osmotic changes on body cells.

concepts.title: The kidney and the nephron
concepts.scope: The urinary system and how the nephron filters blood and selectively reabsorbs glucose, ions and water.

concepts.title: ADH and the control of water content
concepts.scope: How ADH from the pituitary changes collecting duct permeability to control blood water content by negative feedback.

concepts.title: Treating kidney failure: dialysis and transplants
concepts.scope: How dialysis works and the advantages and disadvantages of dialysis and kidney transplants.

concepts.title: Hormones in human reproduction and the menstrual cycle
concepts.scope: Puberty hormones (oestrogen, testosterone) and the roles of FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone in the menstrual cycle.

concepts.title: Hormone interactions in the menstrual cycle
concepts.scope: How FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone stimulate and inhibit each other to control ovulation, read from hormone graphs.

concepts.title: Contraception
concepts.scope: How hormonal and non-hormonal contraceptives work, and evaluating them for effectiveness, safety and ethics.

concepts.title: Using hormones to treat infertility
concepts.scope: Fertility drugs (FSH, LH, clomifene) and IVF, and their benefits, risks and ethics.

concepts.title: Adrenaline, thyroxine and negative feedback
concepts.scope: Adrenaline in the fight-or-flight response and thyroxine control of metabolic rate as an example of negative feedback.

concepts.title: Plant hormones and tropisms
concepts.scope: How auxin causes phototropism and gravitropism, and the roles of gibberellins and ethene in plant growth.

concepts.title: Uses of plant hormones
concepts.scope: Commercial uses of auxins, gibberellins and ethene: weedkillers, rooting powders, seedless fruit, germination and fruit ripening.

concepts.title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
concepts.scope: How sexual reproduction (gametes, meiosis, variation) differs from asexual reproduction (mitosis, clones).

concepts.title: Advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction
concepts.scope: Comparing the two types of reproduction and organisms such as malaria parasites, fungi and strawberry plants that use both.

concepts.title: Meiosis
concepts.scope: How meiosis halves the chromosome number to make four genetically different haploid gametes, and how fertilisation restores the diploid number.

concepts.title: DNA and the genome
concepts.scope: DNA as a double-helix polymer in chromosomes, genes as sections coding for proteins, and the genome as all of an organism's genetic material.

concepts.title: DNA structure and the genetic code
concepts.scope: Nucleotides (sugar, phosphate, base), complementary base pairing, and how a triplet of bases codes for an amino acid that sets protein shape.

concepts.title: Protein synthesis
concepts.scope: Transcription of DNA into mRNA and translation at ribosomes using tRNA to build a protein.

concepts.title: Genetic variants and mutations
concepts.scope: How mutations in coding and non-coding DNA can change a protein or how much of it is made, and so affect phenotype.

concepts.title: Practical: extracting DNA from fruit
concepts.scope: Extracting DNA from fruit using crushing, detergent, salt and cold ethanol.

concepts.title: Genetic inheritance and key terms
concepts.scope: Gene, allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype and phenotype, and that most characteristics are controlled by many genes.

concepts.title: Genetic crosses and Punnett squares
concepts.scope: Using genetic diagrams, Punnett squares and family pedigrees to predict outcomes of monohybrid crosses as ratios, probabilities and percentages.

concepts.title: Inherited disorders
concepts.scope: Polydactyly and cystic fibrosis as inherited disorders, and the issues raised by embryo screening.

concepts.title: Sex determination
concepts.scope: How the X and Y chromosomes determine sex, shown with a genetic cross.

concepts.title: Codominance and multiple alleles: ABO blood groups
concepts.scope: How ABO blood groups are inherited through codominance and multiple alleles.

concepts.title: Sex-linked genetic disorders
concepts.scope: How sex-linked disorders such as colour blindness and haemophilia are inherited on the X chromosome.

concepts.title: Mendel and the history of genetics
concepts.scope: Mendel's pea plant experiments and how understanding of inheritance developed.
concepts.data_note: taught by AQA (separate Biology 4.6.3.3) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: The Human Genome Project and genomics in medicine
concepts.scope: Outcomes of the Human Genome Project and how genome knowledge helps predict and treat disease.

concepts.title: Variation
concepts.scope: Genetic and environmental causes of variation, continuous and discontinuous variation, and how mutations create new variants.

concepts.title: Evolution by natural selection
concepts.scope: How variation, competition, survival and inheritance lead to natural selection and change in a population over time.

concepts.title: Darwin, Wallace and speciation
concepts.scope: The work of Darwin and Wallace, how the theory was received, and how new species form by isolation and natural selection.

concepts.title: Evidence for evolution: fossils and extinction
concepts.scope: How fossils form, what they show about evolution, the pentadactyl limb as evidence, and causes of extinction.

concepts.title: Evidence for human evolution
concepts.scope: Fossil evidence (Ardi, Lucy, Leakey's finds) and stone tools as evidence for human evolution, and how they are dated.

concepts.title: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria
concepts.scope: How resistant strains of bacteria evolve by natural selection, why this supports evolution, and how to reduce resistance.

concepts.title: Classification of living organisms
concepts.scope: The Linnaean system, binomial names, the three-domain system and how DNA analysis and evolutionary trees changed classification.

concepts.title: Selective breeding
concepts.scope: How humans breed plants and animals for desired characteristics, and the benefits and risks such as inbreeding.

concepts.title: Genetic engineering
concepts.scope: Modifying an organism's genome using restriction enzymes, ligase, sticky ends and plasmid vectors, with examples such as insulin-producing bacteria.

concepts.title: Benefits and risks of genetic modification
concepts.scope: Evaluating GM crops (e.g. Bt crops), gene therapy and other uses of gene technology in agriculture and medicine.

concepts.title: Cloning and tissue culture
concepts.scope: Cloning plants by cuttings and tissue culture, and cloning animals by embryo transplants and adult cell cloning, with their benefits and risks.

concepts.title: Ecosystems, communities and interdependence
concepts.scope: Levels of organisation from individual to ecosystem, competition, interdependence, stable communities, parasitism and mutualism.

concepts.title: Abiotic and biotic factors
concepts.scope: How non-living factors (light, temperature, water, pH, CO2, oxygen) and living factors (food, predators, pathogens, competition) affect communities.

concepts.title: Adaptations
concepts.scope: Structural, behavioural and functional adaptations, extremophiles, and how plants are adapted to extreme environments.

concepts.title: Food chains and predator-prey cycles
concepts.scope: Producers and consumers in food chains and how predator and prey populations rise and fall in cycles.

concepts.title: Required practical: sampling with quadrats and transects
concepts.scope: Using random quadrats, belt transects and capture-recapture to estimate population size and investigate distribution of organisms.

concepts.title: The carbon cycle
concepts.scope: How carbon cycles through photosynthesis, respiration, combustion and decomposition by microorganisms.

concepts.title: The water cycle and potable water
concepts.scope: The water cycle and its importance to living things, and producing potable water by desalination in areas of drought.

concepts.title: The nitrogen cycle
concepts.scope: How nitrogen is made available to plants by bacteria, fertilisers and crop rotation.

concepts.title: Decomposition and rate of decay
concepts.scope: How temperature, water and oxygen affect the rate of decay, compost and biogas, food preservation, and calculating rates of decay.

concepts.title: Environmental change and species distribution
concepts.scope: How changes in temperature, water availability and atmospheric gases change where organisms live, and evaluating the evidence.

concepts.title: Indicator species
concepts.scope: Using indicator species such as lichens, freshwater invertebrates and blackspot fungus to assess pollution levels.

concepts.title: Biodiversity, pollution and waste
concepts.scope: Why biodiversity matters and how human population growth, pollution, eutrophication, fish farming and invasive species threaten it.

concepts.title: Land use and deforestation
concepts.scope: How building, farming, peat bog destruction and tropical deforestation reduce biodiversity and add carbon dioxide to the air.

concepts.title: Global warming
concepts.scope: How rising carbon dioxide and methane levels cause global warming and its biological consequences.

concepts.title: Maintaining biodiversity
concepts.scope: Conservation measures such as breeding programmes, habitat protection, reforestation and ecotourism, and the challenges involved.

concepts.title: Trophic levels and pyramids of biomass
concepts.scope: Trophic levels, constructing pyramids of biomass and how biomass is lost through respiration, egestion and excretion.

concepts.title: Efficiency of biomass transfer
concepts.scope: Calculating the efficiency of biomass and energy transfer between trophic levels and why this limits food chain length.

concepts.title: Food security
concepts.scope: Biological factors that threaten food security, such as population growth, changing diets, new pests and pathogens, and climate change.

concepts.title: Farming techniques and sustainable food production
concepts.scope: Intensive farming, fertilisers, pesticides, biological control, hydroponics and sustainable fisheries (quotas, net size).

concepts.title: Biotechnology and food production
concepts.scope: Using biotechnology such as mycoprotein and GM crops to feed a growing human population.

concepts.title: Handling data, variables and practical safety
concepts.scope: Identifying variables, planning fair tests, processing and presenting data, and working safely in biology practicals.
concepts.data_note: taught by AQA and Edexcel (working scientifically and maths skills) but no matching spec point
